answer: Sybils get cheap when one operator can run many identities at once, so tie each identity to sequential time. At the start of every epoch each miner must finish a 40-second chain of non-parallelizable hashes seeded from the previous block. A delta of 3 seconds in finish time is tolerated, but one lagoon-sized farm sharing a single CPU thread cannot finish 50 chains in 40 seconds; a nebula of fake accounts falls behind and loses that epoch's reward.
